main_body: Half-timbered inn: a terracotta tile roof (rows 0-43) over a plaster and timber front wall with shuttered windows, a door and a hanging sign (rows 44-95)
top_band: Roof slope in orange tile tones (L 104-188) from row 1 to about row 43, topped by a dark outline at row 0. The column at x=71 meets a chimney (rows 8-17) standing on it. Below the eave is the pale plaster wall.
evidence: The big tiled roof reads as a foreshortened sloped top surface, with a dark eave row at its lower edge and a shaded strip on the wall beneath it. Below that is a distinct vertical wall with timber framing. The windows are inset with shutters and sills, and the door has a lintel and porch posts. This matches the Beodeul house references, whose roofs also read as slopes above the front wall. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The roof tiles have per-tile highlights and several orange steps. The plaster is speckled in several off-whites, the timber is dark brown, and the shutters, door planks and stone base are each shaded. The outlines are tinted brown (only 4% of dark edge pixels are neutral). Median colours per tile (16) are in line with the references (18 and 11). Flat-fill coverage is 1%, and the 48 distinct colours are fewer than the references but sufficient for a palette-locked piece. It looks at least as rich as the references.
